sense: power over what others think and do
also: have a lot of influence with

terms.gloss: influence, weight, prestige: the standing that makes others follow
evidence: Cic. Lael. 13: plūs apud mē antīquōrum auctōritās valet
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “might, power, authority, reputation, dignity, influence, weight (very freq.)”. It counts with someone: auctōritās valet apud aliquem.

terms.gloss: influence won by favour and connections
evidence: Caes. BG 7.63.1: quantum grātiā, auctōritāte, pecūniā valent
Caes. BG 1.9.3: grātiā et largītiōne … plūrimum poterat

terms.grammar: phrase: apud with the accusative of those influenced; plūs, plūrimum for more and most
evidence: Cic. Lael. 13: plūs apud mē … valet
Cic. Rosc. Am. 4: quī apud mē … plūrimum possunt (Lewis & Short s.v. possum)
Traupman 161: multum valent, they have a lot of clout
terms.comment: The usual way to say that someone has influence: how much he can do, or how much he counts, with others. With the person, apud and the accusative; Plautus also has in and the accusative, “over” (quae in mē plūs potest, Plaut. Truc. 4.2.42, Lewis & Short). Traupman gives in with the ablative, which Lewis & Short does not show with a person.

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation; with ut and the subjunctive, or ad
evidence: Caes. BG 1.3.1: hīs rēbus adductī … cōnstituērunt
terms.comment: In the passive, of the reasons that move someone: hīs rēbus adductus, influenced by these considerations.

evidence: Hor. Ars 163: cēreus in vitium flectī
Cic. Phil. 1.35: sed quid tē ōrātiōne flectam? (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to bend (in opinion or in will), to move, persuade, prevail upon”.

phrases.latin: plūs apud mē antīquōrum auctōritās valet
phrases.english: the authority of the ancients carries more weight with me

phrases.latin: Hīs rēbus adductī et auctōritāte … permōtī cōnstituērunt ea quae ad proficīscendum pertinērent comparāre
phrases.english: Influenced by these considerations and moved by (Orgetorix’s) authority, they decided to get ready what they needed for the journey

phrases.latin: quantum grātiā, auctōritāte, pecūniā valent, ad sollicitandās cīvitātēs nītuntur
phrases.english: with all the influence, authority and money they have, they set about stirring up the states

phrases.latin: inberbus juvenis tandem custōde remōtō gaudet equīs canibusque et aprīcī grāmine Campī, cēreus in vitium flectī, monitōribus asper
phrases.english: the beardless youth, his tutor gone at last, delights in horses and hounds and the grass of the sunny Campus: soft as wax to be shaped to vice, rough with those who advise him
